checks: Persistent same-directory JSON registry binds ledger head digest and count to consumed custody and transition IDs/nonces/intent digests
Initial registry enrollment requires externally provisioned issuer and holder key fingerprints and epoch, but independently authenticated sources are not available
Registry inspection and custody append take one Linux process-owned exclusive lock and reject missing, corrupt, stale or pending registry states
Signed revocation amendment requires separately pre-pinned P-256 authority, root/operator/admin separation, strictly increasing epoch and monotonic key revocations
Journal is appended/fsynced/read back under lock; registry temp file is fsynced and atomically renamed with directory fsync under same lock
An interrupted two-file journal/registry update will block subsequent admission until independently adjudicated rather than silently reset consumed history
limitations: Not an atomic two-file transaction; crashes can leave journal and registry divergent; subsequent admission is refused but no automatic recovery exists
Both local files can be jointly rolled back by a hostile administrator without independently retained external checkpoint
Revocation approvals still depend on externally provisioned pins and a caller-supplied authenticity flag, which does not prove real-world independence
Registry file and lock paths require trusted local directory; no distributed/quorum or cross-host fencing
Signed rotation, revocation and replay control remains documentary and no authenticated original physical evidence has been supplied
Authored Rust tests, GitHub Actions success and live Pages execution unverified
